title: BambooHR Pricing: Core, Pro and Elite Plans (2026)
summary: BambooHR pricing varies by plan and company size, with quoted rates as starting points.
body_markdown:
## Connect BambooHR to other apps with Activepieces


Activepieces watches for events in BambooHR and triggers work in other apps, reaching any of its 747 integrations from a single flow under an MIT-licensed core. It doesn't replace any BambooHR plan or module, so it changes what you buy only at the edges.


Once you have totals from all four vendors, it's worth checking whether a paid add-on is really just a connection you could build yourself.


### Counting workflow runs per month


Count events per month before you count anything else, because an Activepieces workflow is a trigger followed by steps, and the unit it meters is the run: one credit, however many steps that run contains.


Take from it that a single hire fans out into several actions, and all of them sit inside the one credit that run costs.


#### Why the hire record stays the source of truth


The practical gain is that the hire record stays the one source of truth. HR enters the person once in BambooHR; the flow carries the name, start date and manager to the chat tool and the directory.


Without the flow, someone retypes those fields in two other systems, or you pay a vendor's integration fee to have it done for you.


#### Modeling the run volume


What follows from the diagram is a modeling task. Multiply your expected hires by one credit per run, then add the same for terminations and role changes, because each event type is its own flow.


Then compare that figure against what the equivalent paid add-on or integration tier costs you.


Activepieces' core is MIT-licensed and free to self-host, and its free cloud plan includes **1,000 credits a month** , so the automation costs nothing until your runs pass that allowance.


### When BambooHR's native integrations are enough


If the app you need already has a native BambooHR integration that covers the fields and events you care about, use it and skip a second tool.


A separate workflow platform is one more system to maintain, monitor and fix when a field name changes, and that upkeep belongs in your cost model.


Native connections tend to be enough when the job is a single, standard hand-off, such as syncing employee records to a payroll or benefits provider.


Activepieces earns its place when you need logic that no single native integration provides. That means a branch, a condition or a sequence across several of its 747 integrations, or a native route that sits behind a higher tier than you'd otherwise need.


A quick test: list the hand-offs you need, mark which ones a native integration handles on the plan you're already considering, and price only the remainder in Activepieces, at one credit per run and 10,000 credits a month on the $20 Plus plan, revealing whether you should actually invest in external integration, since you'll have the actual costs.


If that remainder is empty, you have nothing to add.
